name: OK-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Longtime incumbent Tom Cole with $2.6M war chest
Democratic challenger raised only $65K with $4K on hand
model.rationale: Cole is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by 17 points, while challenger Mitchell Jacob has raised minimal money and has almost no cash on hand. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Cole win, so the forecast stays near the baseline.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending surge for Jacob or an unexpected Cole scandal could narrow the margin, though a true upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 17 points toward the GOP. Tom Cole, a veteran incumbent, is seeking another term and holds a decisive financial advantage: he has raised roughly $3.8 million and has $2.6 million on hand, plus modest outside support. His Democratic challenger, Mitchell Jacob, has raised about $65,000 with only a few thousand dollars left, and an independent candidate is also on the ballot but shows no measurable support.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and incumbency, all of which favor Cole heavily. Prediction markets give Cole about a 94% chance of winning. The expected margin is a comfortable Republican victory in the high teens, with little evidence suggesting a competitive race.
